gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_mmio survey reviewable without claiming a transport implementation.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, bounded queue descriptor-shape metadata, notification accounting, and config-change disposition summaries, so the MMIO lane should build on that real foothold instead of inventing a second core starter.
The live repo now also ships a dedicated virtio-core survey gate, so the MMIO lane should count the full Phase 10 virtio survey surface instead of freezing the older six-file snapshot.
The core survey note now records the current virtio-core gap against the roadmap, which gives the MMIO survey a fuller and more current upstream lane reference before transport work begins.
The existing ring survey keeps the landed queue-discipline surface and the remaining MMIO ladder explicit, which the MMIO lane depends on before broader transport-facing work can honestly begin.

The live repo now has a tiny in-memory virtqueue helper for queue shape, notification bookkeeping, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable state, delayed-callback pacing, and queue reset discipline, so the MMIO lane can survey the remaining transport gap against a real queue-facing foothold.
The ring slice note records the bounded queue-helper surface and its remaining non-goals, which keeps the MMIO lane from overstating transport readiness.
A dedicated MMIO survey gate keeps the remaining transport gap explicit and reviewable now that the queue-address, config-window, config-write, interrupt-ack, and probe-preflight helpers have landed.

The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the current MMIO transport scope and the reasons the broader transport lifecycle work is still blocked even after the register-window, queue-register, queue-notify, queue-address, config-window, config-write, interrupt-ack, and probe-preflight helpers landed.

The MMIO helper needs its slice note to stay focused on the bounded register-window, queue-register, queue-notify, queue-address, config-window, config-write, interrupt-state summary, interrupt-ack, and probe-preflight surface rather than the full transport driver.

The live virtio_ring helper now covers queue shape, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable, delayed-callback pacing, and queue reset discipline, so the MMIO lane no longer needs to hold the ring-local follow-up open.

The roadmap requires virtqueue wrappers ahead of MMIO work, and that prerequisite is now satisfied by the landed virtio_ring delayed-callback pacing step, so the first honest MMIO follow-up is this bounded transport-identity and register-window helper, keeping magic-value, transport-version, device-id, and vendor-id bookkeeping reviewable before broader queue or lifecycle claims.

The live repo now has bounded MMIO feature-page, status, config-generation, and interrupt-ack bookkeeping, so the next honest follow-up is this queue-register planning helper around queue select, queue size bounds, and ready-state bookkeeping rather than probe, remove, or DMA-facing transport work.

With queue select, queue size, and queue ready planning now modeled in-memory, the next bounded MMIO follow-up was a tiny queue-notify snapshot helper, and the live helper now records notify bookkeeping without claiming broader queue setup, IRQ delivery, DMA plumbing, or lifecycle glue.

With queue-notify bookkeeping now reviewable, the live MMIO helper now also ships a version-scoped queue-address planning helper around legacy PFN versus modern DESC, AVAIL, and USED register windows without claiming shared interrupt delivery, probe, or remove lifecycle work.

With queue-address planning now landed, the next honest bounded MMIO follow-up was a tiny config-window snapshot helper, and the live helper still records those read-side snapshots against the current config-generation as the base that the now-landed config-write planning helper builds on without claiming queue setup, IRQ delivery, or lifecycle glue.

After bounded config-window snapshots landed, the live MMIO helper now also carries a tiny config-write planning helper that records previous and planned values for byte, halfword, and word config-window rewrites while keeping config-generation explicit and without claiming full config-space parity, queue setup, IRQ delivery, probe, or remove lifecycle work.

With bounded interrupt-state summaries already landed, the live MMIO helper now also records explicit interrupt-status acknowledge bookkeeping for the reviewable queue and config interrupt bits, keeping the in-memory clear path separate from shared IRQ delivery or lifecycle claims.

With transport-identity snapshots and bounded interrupt-ack bookkeeping already landed, the live MMIO helper can now keep the earliest `virtio_mmio_probe()` gate reviewable through a tiny preflight summary around magic, version, device, vendor, legacy guest-page-size intent, queue-register-window readiness, and interrupt-ack readiness without claiming probe or remove lifecycle, IRQ delivery, or DMA parity.

Broader `virtio_mmio.c` parity still mixes interrupt acknowledgement, queue setup, queue notify side effects, config-space writes, reset, and probe or remove lifecycle paths, which remain too transport-facing to claim even after the bounded register-window, queue-register, queue-notify, queue-address, config-window, config-write, interrupt-ack, and probe-preflight helpers are landed.
